Affiliation:: School of Chemical, Biological and Materials Engineering / School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, The University of Oklahoma
Techniques Used: Interband optical transition energy gap calculation
Application Areas: Trace Gas Sensing for Clinical Diagnostics
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Quantum Confinement Engineering for Bandgap Optimization: Utilizing multiple quantum well (MQW) structures in IV-VI semiconductors to remove L-valley degeneracy and reduce effective density of states, thereby lowering intrinsic carrier concentrations and enhancing open-circuit voltage in thermophotovoltaic devices.

Multi-Junction Current Matching for Efficiency Maximization: Designing dual- or triple-junction TPV architectures with optimized layer thicknesses to balance short-circuit current densities across junctions, achieving power conversion efficiencies up to 35.7% and power densities exceeding 4 W/cm² when coupled with high-temperature radiators.

Non-Invasive Metabolomic Gas-Phase Sensing: Employing mid-infrared interband cascade laser absorption spectroscopy to detect volatile organic compounds (e.g., acetaldehyde) in bioreactor headspace, enabling real-time monitoring of hypoxia-driven metabolic shifts in cancer cell cultures without invasive sampling.

Thermodynamic-Economic System Integration: Coupling theoretical performance modeling of solid-state energy conversion devices with levelized cost of energy (LCOE) calculations to demonstrate the viability of molten silicon thermal storage systems as competitive, low-cost solutions for grid-scale renewable energy integration.
Summary Description: Patrick McCann is a multidisciplinary researcher specializing in advanced energy conversion systems and bioanalytical sensing. His work leverages narrow-gap IV-VI semiconductor multiple quantum well structures to develop high-efficiency thermophotovoltaic (TPV) devices for thermal energy grid storage. By engineering quantum confinement effects to optimize band structures and matching multi-junction currents, he achieves significant improvements in power density and conversion efficiency, targeting low-cost decarbonization. Concurrently, he applies mid-infrared laser absorption spectroscopy to monitor metabolic byproducts in cancer cell cultures, providing non-invasive insights into hypoxia-driven metabolic shifts. This dual focus bridges solid-state physics and analytical chemistry to address critical challenges in renewable energy storage and clinical diagnostics.
